refrain: Glory be to You, our God, glory be to You!
comment:
Three-ode in Tone 2.
It is modeled on the Holy Monday and Holy Tuesday Three-odes and has acrostics: "To Monday" and "To Tuesday".
(Shortening the canon will remove the repetitions while keeping all parts.)

odes.hirmos: Let us sing to the Lord* Who drained impassible and tumultuous sea by His divine order,* and taught Israel to pass through it on foot,* for gloriously has He been glorified.
troparia: The condescension of the Word of God is beyond words, for Christ is understood as the God-Man: He is God not by elevation, and is revealed to us as an image of a servant - for gloriously has He been glorified.

Christ comes voluntarily to serve to impoverished Adam, whose image He, his Creator, now takes upon Himself, enriching him with Divinity, and granting him a wondrous renewal and regeneration as the Compassionate One.

odes.hirmos: The fire, kindled beyond measure and unrestrained,* was driven back by the bodies of the pious Youths, as pure as their souls.* And when the ever-living flame was quenched,* a never-ceasing canticle was raised:* O all you works of the Lord, hymn the Lord* and supremely exalt Him throughout all ages!
troparia: “You shall all be My kindred, if you keep My commandments,” says Christ to humanity, He who passed through the womb of the Immaculate One. He now grants peace and teaches men to think humbly of themselves. And He adds: “Praise and supremely exalt Me, whom you know as the Lord, throughout all ages.”

O Word of God, Nativity in the flesh is adverse to Your nature: it was not flesh and blood that formed Your holy Body, but the coming of the Holy Spirit and the overshadowing of the Most High. Therefore, acknowledging You as the Lord, we praise and supremely exalt You throughout all ages.”
Let us cast far from us slothfulness, and with vigilant souls meet Christ Who is born of the pure Virgin, crying: O all you works of the Lord, bless the Lord.
May good deeds be a sufficient treasure for our souls, so that with radiant faces we may sing: O all you works of the Lord, bless the Lord.
Let us, having cultivated a talent of good works, bring it to Christ Who is to be born of the Virgin, the Handmaiden of God.
odes.katavasia:
The three holy children were not obedient* to the decree of the tyrant;* and, cast into the furnace, they confessed God, singing:* O, all you works of the Lord, bless the Lord.
(we bow)

odes.hirmos:
You have magnified, O Christ, the Theotokos who bore You:* from her, O our Creator, You took a body sharing our passions similar to ours,* and delivered us from all our transgressions.* Wherefore with all generations we call her blessed and we magnify You.
(we bow)
troparia: Having cast away all the impurity of the passions, let us worthily receive Christ's coming with sound minds, as He is comes blamelessly to bear flesh and to grant all divine renewal in the Spirit.

Beholding Christ humbling Himself, let us rise above lowly passions. Let us not think highly but, instructed in the faith, be humble in spirit, that we may exalt with high deeds Him, Who is to be born.
Christ commands those of sound mind who await His coming from the Virgin to keep watch. Behold, the Lord is coming to be born!
At Your second coming, O Christ, number me among Your sheep, as I venerate Your coming in the flesh.
odes.katavasia:
You contained within your womb* the God whom nothing can contain,* and have brought forth joy to the world,* wherefore we sing your praises, O Virgin Theotokos.
(we bow)
